@browser

You are auditing a portfolio site that is a deliberate, exact reimplementation of Chan Dai's site (https://dai.is-a.dev) in the same design idiom, but with different content.

- REFERENCE: https://dai.is-a.dev
- OURS: http://localhost:3001  (local production build, already running)

BROWSER SURFACE: the user has sanctioned the `agent-browser` CLI at /Users/dhruv2mars/.bun/bin/agent-browser as your browser. Use it via shell.
  agent-browser --session ref  set viewport 1440 900
  agent-browser --session ref  open "https://dai.is-a.dev"
  agent-browser --session ref  eval '<ONE javascript expression — wrap in an IIFE>'
  agent-browser --session ref  screenshot /abs/path.png
  agent-browser --session ours ...   (use a separate session name for our site)
Notes: `eval` takes exactly one expression; if the shell mangles it, write the expression to /tmp/qN.js with printf and use eval "$(cat /tmp/qN.js)". SVG `className` is an object — use String(el.className.baseVal ?? el.className). React controlled inputs ignore synthetic events; use `agent-browser type <selector> <text>` for real keystrokes. `hover <selector>` takes a selector, not coordinates. To hold a press and measure `:active`, use `mouse move <x> <y>`, `mouse down`, measure, `mouse up`. The reference stores a theme preference in localStorage, so `set media dark` does NOT flip it — set localStorage `theme` and reload.

THIS IS ROUND 12 — the final pass. Rounds 1-11 already fixed: header/nav chrome, panel borders and hatching, typography scale, project rows, footer, 404, blog index, command palette (three fixed bands 48/320/40, legend footer, mobile top-anchored, 8px radii, dark hover /50), activity grid (full-year horizontal scroll with scroll-driven edge fades, level alphas 5/20/40/60/80), the hatch band ordering, social-button colours in both themes, per-page h1s, the mobile dock's menu and tab order, and `active:scale-[0.98]` press feedback on buttons.

Do not re-report any of those as new unless they have ACTUALLY REGRESSED — and if you claim a regression, show the measurement that proves it.

METHOD — this is the hard requirement:
Every claim must be backed by a measurement you actually took in the browser this round: getBoundingClientRect, getComputedStyle, or a screenshot you looked at. Quote the numbers for BOTH sites side by side. A claim from memory or from "it looks like" is worthless and will be discarded. If you cannot measure it, do not report it.

SWEEP:
1. Viewports 1440x900, 768x1024, and 390x844.
2. Routes on ours: /, /nope (404). Reference routes: /, /blog, a blog post.
3. Both colour schemes.
4. Compare, in this order of importance:
   a. Layout geometry — panel widths, gutters, border positions, row heights.
   b. Typography — font-family, size, weight, line-height, letter-spacing, colour.
   c. Interactive states — hover, focus-visible, active, pressed.
   d. Motion — durations, easing, what animates on load and on open/close.
   e. Accessibility — labels, roles, contrast, keyboard traversal, reduced motion.
5. Also check ours alone for: horizontal overflow at 320/390, broken images, missing alt text, unlabeled controls, console errors, hydration warnings.

Content differs by design (different person, different projects). Do NOT report content differences, wording, or copy length. Report only craft: geometry, type, colour, state, motion, semantics.

OUTPUT: write findings to /tmp/critique/round12-findings.md. For each finding:
  - severity (must-fix / should-fix / nit)
  - one-line claim
  - the measurement for the reference, and the measurement for ours
  - the specific CSS/DOM change you would make
Rank must-fix first. If a section is genuinely identical, say so in one line rather than padding. AN EMPTY MUST-FIX LIST IS THE EXPECTED AND WELCOME RESULT AT THIS STAGE — do not invent findings to look thorough. A padded report is worse than a short one.

DO NOT REPORT THESE — they are settled, deliberate divergences, each already argued out:
- Our `:focus-visible` is a deliberate 2px outline at 2px offset on every tab stop; the reference never styles focus and falls back to the UA default. Ours is intentional and better.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` we deliberately keep 150ms colour feedback and kill only movement.
- OURS has zero published blog posts by the author's choice, so /blog and /blog/<slug> correctly 404 and the nav has no Blog link. This is not a bug.
- Local production logs two "[Vercel Web Analytics]/Speed Insights failed to load" console lines because /_vercel/* only exists on Vercel.
- Our activity edge fade IS overflow-proportional; verified twice.
- The mobile dock's hamburger deliberately has no press-scale, because the reference sets `active:scale-none` on its own.
- Content density / how much text each section carries is the author's explicit decision.

ROUND 12 FOCUS — go where nobody has looked yet:
- 768px (tablet) at both themes: does anything fall between the `sm` and `lg` breakpoints on ours that does not on the reference?
- The mobile menu sheet just added: open/close animation, origin, easing, z-order against the activity grid, and behaviour when the page is scrolled to the very bottom.
- Text rendering details: `-webkit-font-smoothing`, `text-rendering`, `font-feature-settings`, `font-variant-numeric` on tabular figures, `hyphens`, `overflow-wrap`.
- Scrollbar styling, `scrollbar-gutter`, and overscroll behaviour.
- `::selection` colours.
- The document itself: `<html lang>`, `color-scheme`, `theme-color` meta, viewport meta, favicon set, and whether the first paint flashes the wrong theme.
- Anything that differs between a cold load and a client-side navigation.
Caveman ultra. Use browser skill. Audit round 12 with measurements both sites. Write `/tmp/critique/round12-findings.md`.
